transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-31
Start: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Amit, Lena, Diego, Sofia, Claire, Evan + all employees

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, happy, uh, end of year. Welcome to the Redwood year-end all-hands. I'm Maya, and we'll kick off with some highlights from 2026 then Amit will walk through our tech priorities, Lena product, and then we'll do Q&A. Quick note: recording is on, chat questions will be pulled in.

[00:38] Evan Brooks: Quick housekeeping - second half we'll open the mic to questions, please keep them concise. Also the Q4 deck will be shared after this call.

[01:05] Maya Chen: Okay, 2026 in review, short version: we grew ARR by 2.3x, Dedicated bookings up 4x, Private pilots doubled, and unit costs per token improved roughly 18% thanks to batching and quantization work. Big shout out to infra and research, that's Sofia and Amit's teams. There were, uh, challenges on latency SLOs in one region in August, but we put fixes in and latency is back within target.

[02:12] Applause (inaudible)

[02:25] Amit Rao: Yeah hi, quick technical recap, 2026 we shipped continuous batching improvements, kernel selection heuristics, and a new experimental KV cache that cut repeated prompt cost by about 35% in internal tests. We also launched our first production-grade quantized model variants for some customers. Important note, those quantized variants trade a small delta in quality for huge cost savings; product teams, please coordinate on canaries.

[03:06] Lena Park: From product side, we focused on three things: reliability features (rollouts, fallback policies), observability (per-route dashboards), and onboarding self-serve. The console improvements cut time-to-first-call for new teams from days to hours. We also shipped the Optimize suggestions beta — early customers reported meaningful cost savings.

[03:55] Sofia Alvarez: Research highlights: our evals platform caught two regressions before they hit prod, and we improved our model ranking signals. Note that model performance varies by workload (long context vs short). We recommend teams run evals on their prompt sets before switching variants.

[04:40] Claire Ng: Security update - our SOC 2 Type II prep is underway, initial gaps are being addressed. We also added KMS integration improvements, better audit logging, and we have a roadmap for ISO compliance in H1 2027. We'll publish details and an audit checklist next week.

[05:10] Diego Martinez: Sales recap: enterprise pipeline closed strong in Q4. We converted three Fortune 100 trials to Dedicated. There's clear demand for Private deployments in regulated verticals. Pricing conversations were mostly about predictable pricing for heavy inference workloads; customers want both latency guarantees and cost predictability.

[05:45] Evan Brooks: Financials — quick numbers, revenue up, but gross margin pressured by higher GPU costs in Q3; optimizations pushed margin back up in Q4. We expect tooling and dedicated capacity adoption to improve margins further in 2027.

[06:15] Maya Chen: Ok moving to 2027 priorities at a high level: 1) Reliability and SLOs (we will invest in routing and graceful degradation), 2) Improving unit economics (more Optimize features, better quantization workflows), 3) Expand Dedicated and Private - we need to make Private easier to deploy and operate, 4) Hiring for infra, product, and sales. We'll say more on hiring in a sec.

[07:05] Crowd noise, a few people typing

[07:20] Amit Rao: Technical priorities bullets: finish Private control plane improvements, automated rollback for canary rollouts, KV-cache productionization, and better autoscaling heuristics. We also plan to reduce median p99 latency by focusing on kernel choice and batching policy per-route. We'll run a deep-dive week of benchmarks in Jan.

[08:05] Lena Park: Product priorities: finish Optimize GA, add more model variant suggestions, improve route-level RBAC in the console, and make rollout templates for common configurations (SLA, cost, privacy). We're also going to provide templates for regulated verticals to ease Private adoption.

[08:45] Claire Ng: On compliance, immediate tasks: SOC/ISO checklist, roll out mandatory security training for engineering, and publish retention/archival policies for customer data.

[09:15] Maya Chen: Hiring - we plan to add ~45 roles next quarter across infra, product, and sales. People Ops will publish the plan. We're prioritizing senior infra and reliability engineers. Please refer candidates internally. 

[09:55] Question (Chat): "Will there be price changes for hosted API in 2027?"

[10:03] Evan Brooks: Short answer: no across-the-board price increase planned. We'll continue to offer discounts for committed Dedicated capacity and pilot programs for Private. That said, we will introduce a new tiered unit pricing for extremely high-volume customers to keep costs sustainable for the business. Details in the Q4 deck.

[10:40] Question (Shannon, Sales): "How should AE/SE position quantized variants to customers concerned about regressions?"

[10:47] Amit Rao: Recommend canarying on a representative eval set, run both variants, measure key metrics. Use our evals dashboard and if quality impact is unacceptable, fall back automatically using rollout policies. Also mention cost delta and provide example cases where quantization is appropriate (non-critical summarization, embeddings-heavy pipelines).

[11:30] Question (Terry, Eng): "Private deployment complexity — timeline and support model?"

[11:38] Maya Chen: We're doubling down here. The product + infra teams have a roadmap to reduce deployment time by automating network and KMS integration. Timeline: we aim for a much smoother Private GA experience in H1 2027. Amit will host a deep-dive and benchmark session next month.

[12:10] Slight crosstalk, someone drops audio

[12:30] Open Q&A — mixed rapid-fire questions: support for multi-region fallbacks, observability retention pricing, and whether we'll open-source any infra tools.

[13:05] Amit Rao: On open-sourcing, we remain supportive of open tools but will be selective — we can't open-source everything that makes our managed offering differentiated. We'll consider tooling that benefits the ecosystem without revealing sensitive ops logic.

[14:00] Lena Park: Observability retention - we'll offer premium retention as an add-on; default retention will be shorter to control infra costs.

[14:25] Claire Ng: Multi-region failover - we support routing by region and automatic fallback; we're improving the orchestration so failover is faster and preserves KV cache where possible. There are trade-offs between latency and state sync, we'll document patterns.

[15:10] Random applause

[15:25] Maya Chen: Alright, final notes: maintain focus on shipping the roadmap, coordinate closely on Private customer pilots, and please read the Q4 deck when it's out. Thanks for all the hard work in 2026, big year. See you all in 2027.

[15:50] Meeting end - quick hallway chatter, people start leaving the room

Notes on transcription quality: Some overlap and speaker labels are approximate, occasional mis-transcribed words (e.g., KVcache vs K V cache). Links mentioned during the meeting: Q4 metrics deck (internal link), Private roadmap doc (internal link), SOC checklist (internal link).
